Class Native

java.lang.Object
smile.torch.Native
public final class Native extends Object
Internal helpers for the FFM (Foreign Function and Memory API) binding to the smile_torch native library. This class glues the idiomatic smile.deep.tensor API to the raw smile_torch_h downcall stubs generated by jextract.

It centralizes three concerns: converting native error sentinels into Java exceptions, freeing native handles when their Java wrappers become unreachable (via a shared Cleaner), and a handful of downcalls for functions that are not yet covered by the generated bindings.

    • CLEANER

      public static final Cleaner CLEANER
      Shared cleaner that releases native handles owned by Java wrappers (tensors, indices, modules, …) once those wrappers are no longer reachable. It is a safety net; callers should still close resources deterministically via try-with-resources or an AutoScope where possible.

    • cudaMemGetInfo

      public static long[] cudaMemGetInfo(int deviceIndex)
      Queries free and total CUDA device memory via LibTorch's caching allocator (cudaMemGetInfo under a device guard).

      Requires a smile_torch binary built with USE_CUDA (CUDA Toolkit + CUDA LibTorch). A CPU-only build fails with a clear native error rather than a silent -1.

      Parameters:
      deviceIndex - the CUDA device index.
      Returns:
      long[2] of {freeBytes, totalBytes}.
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the query fails (e.g. CUDA unavailable).

    • cudaAllocatorStats

      public static long[] cudaAllocatorStats(int deviceIndex)
      Queries CUDACachingAllocator live vs reserved bytes for a device.

      allocated is storage owned by live tensors; reserved is the cudaMalloc footprint (includes free cached blocks that Device.emptyCache() can return to the driver).

      Parameters:
      deviceIndex - the CUDA device index.
      Returns:
      long[2] of {allocatedBytes, reservedBytes}.
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - if the query fails.

    • flashInferAttentionPagedRaw

      public static Tensor flashInferAttentionPagedRaw(Tensor query, Tensor kCache, Tensor vCache, Tensor kvIndptr, Tensor kvIndices, Tensor kvLastPageLen, int pageSize, int numKvHeads, int headDim, int cacheLen, double scale, boolean isCausal, Tensor mask, MemorySegment workspace)
      Raw-tensor paged attention (existing eager S==1/S>1 dispatch), bypassing AttentionContext/KvCachePool.

      Exists so a Stage 1 (SMILE_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH) smoke test can compare flashInferAttentionVerifyCapturable(Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, int, int, int, int, double, float, float, boolean, MemorySegment)'s output against this existing, proven path on identical raw tensors, without needing to stand up the full production KV-pool machinery. flashInferAttention(Tensor, Tensor, AttentionContext) is the production entry point built on the same underlying call; this is a thin sibling at the same tensor-level boundary.

      Parameters:
      query - query [B, Hq, S, D]
      kCache - key cache [numSlots, Hkv, D] (one layer slice)
      vCache - value cache [numSlots, Hkv, D]
      kvIndptr - int32 [B+1]
      kvIndices - int32 [numPages]
      kvLastPageLen - int32 [B]
      pageSize - tokens per page
      numKvHeads - Hkv
      headDim - D
      cacheLen - total sequence length (for CSR validation; 0 to skip)
      scale - attention scale (<= 0 → 1/sqrt(D))
      isCausal - whether to apply causal masking; ignored (SDPA requires the caller not set both) when mask != null
      mask - optional explicit additive mask, e.g. [S, cacheLen] (broadcastable); pass non-null for "continuation window" causal semantics (bottom-right-aligned: column j valid for row i iff j <= i + (cacheLen - S)) — plain isCausal=true with no mask uses PyTorch SDPA's own is_causal, which is top-left-aligned for S != cacheLen and therefore wrong for this use case. May be null.
      workspace - FlashInfer workspace handle
      Returns:
      output [B, Hq, S, D]

    • flashInferAttentionVerifyCapturable

      public static Tensor flashInferAttentionVerifyCapturable(Tensor query, Tensor kCache, Tensor vCache, Tensor qoIndptr, Tensor kvIndptr, Tensor kvIndices, Tensor kvLastPageLen, int pageSize, int numKvHeads, int headDim, int qoLen, double scale, float kScale, float vScale, boolean isCausal, MemorySegment workspace)
      Stage 1 (SMILE_VERIFY_CUDA_GRAPH): graph-capturable multi-token (S>1) causal paged attention for MTP window verify (see smile_flashinfer_paged_attention_verify_cuda). Isolated sibling of flashInferAttention(Tensor, Tensor, AttentionContext) — not wired into the live verify path yet; this exists so Stage 1's eager-mode correctness can be validated directly against flashInferAttention(Tensor, Tensor, AttentionContext)'s existing SDPA path before any later stage touches Qwen/QwenModel.

      No additive mask parameter (FlashInfer's masking here is compile-time MaskMode, unlike the additive-mask SDPA path).

      Parameters:
      query - query [B, Hq, S, D]
      kCache - key cache [numSlots, Hkv, D] (one layer slice)
      vCache - value cache [numSlots, Hkv, D]
      qoIndptr - int32 [B+1], values {0,S,2S,...}
      kvIndptr - int32 [B+1]
      kvIndices - int32 [numPages]
      kvLastPageLen - int32 [B]
      pageSize - tokens per page
      numKvHeads - Hkv
      headDim - D
      qoLen - S (must equal query's 3rd dim)
      scale - attention scale (<= 0 → 1/sqrt(D))
      kScale - FP8 KV key dequant scale (1.0 when KV is bf16/fp16)
      vScale - FP8 KV value dequant scale (1.0 when KV is bf16/fp16)
      isCausal - diagnostic-only toggle (MaskMode::kCausal vs kNone); production callers always pass true
      workspace - FlashInfer workspace handle
      Returns:
      output [B, Hq, S, D]

    • flashInferAttentionVerifyGraph

      public static Tensor flashInferAttentionVerifyGraph(Tensor query, AttentionContext ctx, Tensor qoIndptr)
      Production entry point for the graph-capturable MTP window-verify kernel, built on AttentionContext (KV pool layer slice + CSR + workspace) — the verify-graph sibling of flashInferAttention(Tensor, Tensor, AttentionContext), targeting smile_flashinfer_paged_attention_verify instead of smile_flashinfer_paged_attention. ctx.isCausal() must be true (this kernel has no additive-mask parameter; causal masking is the compile-time, bottom-right-aligned MaskMode::kCausal validated in Stage 1/2).
      Parameters:
      query - query [B, Hq, S, D]
      ctx - paged context with pool + CSR + workspace (seqLen is the query window length)
      qoIndptr - int32 [B+1], values {0,S,2S,...} (KvCachePool.verifyQoIndptrBuf(int, int))
      Returns:
      output [B, Hq, S, D]

    • flashInferAttentionVerifyEager

      public static Tensor flashInferAttentionVerifyEager(Tensor query, AttentionContext ctx, Tensor qoIndptr)
      Verify attention for calls that are not part of a CUDA graph bucket (eager verify windows, batched/ragged verify). Plans into a scratch workspace disjoint from flashInferAttentionVerifyGraph(Tensor, AttentionContext, Tensor)'s, so a captured graph's baked plan arrays can never be overwritten by an eager plan of a different shape. Falls back to the graph entry point on an older native library.
